land.text: the north-western strip of Lazica, the Black Sea coast between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers (Cliopatria's Georgia row, 724-777)

predecessors.note: The Abasgia page: Abasgia 'was originally part of the Kingdom of Lazica', its rulers were 'appointed by the kings of Lazica, probably upon the approval of the Byzantine emperor'; infobox 'Preceded by: Colchis; Lazica'. The dossier starts in 724, the year Cliopatria's Georgia row begins and the kingdom-of-lazica dossier books the loss, not at the infobox's 64.

land.text: Abasgia, which Leon II made the core of the Kingdom of Abkhazia ('King of the Abkhazians') when he won his full independence c. 778

successors.note: The Abasgia infobox gives 'Disestablished: 786' and 'Succeeded by: Kingdom of Abkhazia'; the Kingdom of Abkhazia page gives independence c. 778 and the capital Anacopia 778-786. This dossier ends in 777 so the kingdom starts in 778 without an overlap.

capitals.name: Anacopia (Anakopia, New Athos)
capitals.note: Abasgia infobox: 'Capital: Anacopia', the only one listed. Coordinates are those the kingdom-of-abkhazia dossier uses for Anacopia (New Athos); the page gives none.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Georgia row 724-777 (7,076 km2, bbox 39.1-41.6E, 42.9-44.2N) is the Abasgian land; shape unchanged, read as the Principality of Abasgia, 'territory between Gumista and Bzyb rivers'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria files the 7,076 km2 coastal shape under the Name 'Georgia', which belongs to another dossier (it is not Georgia the state). The Abasgia page has no area and no boundary; it says Abasgia 'occupied territory between Gumista and Bzyb rivers' (4th century) and gives only Anacopia as a place. The shape runs from the Gumista area north to about 44.2 N, far beyond the Bzyb through the Sochi coast, so the page supports the Abkhaz core and not the Russian part of the strip; the reviewer may trim it to the Abkhazia admin-1. Accepted at the honest precision of the era.

region.text: Anacopia (New Athos) and the coast between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers

ledger.note: 724: the Abasgian principality stands on the Abkhaz coast at Anacopia, a Byzantine dependency. The Abasgia page is silent on 724: it gives the 4th-century occupation of 'territory between Gumista and Bzyb rivers', the infobox 'Established: 64' and 'Capital: Anacopia'; 724 is the year Cliopatria's Georgia shape begins and the kingdom-of-lazica dossier books the loss. Kingdom of Abkhazia page: 'Abkhazia was a princedom under Byzantine authority' whose archon 'effectively functioned as a Byzantine viceroy'.

region.text: the Black Sea coast between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers and its hinterland, as Cliopatria draws it (its Georgia row, 724-777, 7,076 km2)

ledger.note: 724: the north-western coast passes to the Abasgians in the record. The Abasgia page says the principality 'was originally part of the Kingdom of Lazica' and gives no date for a transfer; the date and shape are Cliopatria's (Georgia row from 724), carried in the kingdom-of-lazica ledger as a loss to 'kingdom-of-abkhazia' (that counterpart should read principality-of-abasgia).

region.text: the Black Sea coast between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers and its hinterland, as Cliopatria draws it (its Georgia row, 724-777, 7,076 km2)

ledger.note: c. 778: Leon II wins full independence from Byzantium and the principality becomes the Kingdom of Abkhazia. 'Towards circa 778, Leon II won his full independence with the help of the Khazars.' The Abasgia infobox gives 'Disestablished: 786' and the Kingdom of Abkhazia page says the state 'was established in the 780s'; the dossier ends in 777 to match the Cliopatria row and the kingdom dossier's 778 start.

wars.name: Arab expedition of Marwan ibn Muhammad into Abkhazia
wars.outcome: The Arab army 'surged into Abkhazia in 736' but, hit by dysentery and floods and meeting 'a stubborn resistance offered by the archon Leon I and his Iberian and Lazic allies', retreated; no border moved.
wars.note: The Leon I page dates the expedition 'In 735'; the Kingdom of Abkhazia page has the invasion of Abkhazia in 736. The pages do not say the Arabs held ground, so no contest is recorded. Listed as the one dated fight inside the dossier's life.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the Abasgia page names two rivers (Gumista and Bzyb) and one town (Anacopia); the Cliopatria strip is soft throughout.

sources.title: Abasgia

sources.title: Kingdom of Abkhazia

sources.title: Leon I of Abkhazia
sources.note: Title of archon from Leo III, the 735 expedition, rule over Egrisi, Jiketi and Sanigia accepted by the Byzantines; reign dates uncertain ('720-740, or c. 745-767').

notes: Requested by the p0700-p0799 window: the Cliopatria Georgia row 724-777 (7,076 km2) is the principality and no dossier held it. The Abasgia page is thin for the 8th century (it ends its narrative with the 550 rising, the 551 restoration of Byzantine control and an undated end-of-the-8th-century independence); the Kingdom of Abkhazia and Leon I pages supply the 735/736 Arab invasion and c. 778. Start year: the infobox says Established 64 but no sentence on the page gives 64 or any founding event, and the kingdom-of-lazica dossier (loss at 724) draws the coast as Lazic land before; the dossier therefore starts at 724 (conf. 1 found and gain, Cliopatria's year) and a gap-filler with a page for 64-723 could extend it backwards as a Lazic or Byzantine dependency. Byzantine suzerainty (archon, 'Byzantine viceroy') and the Khazar help of c. 778 are not in this ledger because vassal events belong in the suzerain's ledger: byzantine-empire should carry a vassal_start/vassal_end for Abasgia (counterpart principality-of-abasgia). The kingdom-of-lazica ledger's loss at 724 names counterpart kingdom-of-abkhazia where it should say principality-of-abasgia, and kingdom-of-abkhazia's found event at 778 already names principality-of-abasgia. Rulers omitted: the infobox lists names without reliable dates and the Leon I page gives '720-740, or c. 745-767'. Cliopatria shape runs north of the Bzyb to 44.2 N (Sochi to Tuapse): unsupported by any page opened. Georgia row 724-777 is reviewed here as a new keyframe, not under georgia.json.
